session.question: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
session.answer:
Combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF improves hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) diagnosis by outperforming either marker alone in overall diagnostic reliability. KAI1 alone had strong diagnostic performance, with an AUC (area under the ROC curve) of 0.907, 86.96% sensitivity, and 83.06% accuracy, whereas VEGF alone had a lower AUC of 0.779. When the two markers were assessed together, sensitivity increased to 91.86%, accuracy rose to 84.68%, and negative predictive value improved to 78.79%, indicating better case detection and fewer missed HCC cases. The study therefore supports combined KAI1+VEGF testing as a more reliable biomarker panel than single-marker testing for HCC diagnosis. (zhang2014expressioncharacteristicsof chunk 1)

The available excerpt does not provide combined specificity, so the improvement is best characterized in terms of sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value rather than a full diagnostic profile. (zhang2014expressioncharacteristicsof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-47c7603b: The study reports that serum KAI1 is downregulated and VEGF is upregulated in HCC. For diagnosis, KAI1 alone had a higher ROC AUC (0.907) than VEGF alone (0.779). Serum KAI1 alone showed 86.96% sensitivity and 83.06% accuracy for HCC detection. When KAI1 and VEGF were combined, diagnostic performance improved: sensitivity increased to 91.86%, accuracy to 84.68%, and negative predictive value to 78.79%. The authors conclude that combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF provides a more reliable diagnostic panel for HCC than either marker alone, though the excerpt does not provide combined specificity values.
From Wu Zhang, Cheng-Guang Zhao, Hong-Yu Sun, Wei-E Zheng, and Hua Chen. Expression characteristics of kai1 and vascular endothelial growth factor and their diagnostic value for hepatocellular carcinoma. Gut and Liver, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.5009/gnl13331, doi:10.5009/gnl13331.

pqac-cf0e90d7: The study found that KAI1 is downregulated and VEGF is upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues and serum. Serum KAI1 levels correlated with TNM stage and metastatic features; VEGF was also associated with AFP level. For diagnosis, KAI1 alone had an AUC of 0.907 with 86.96% sensitivity and 83.06% accuracy, while VEGF alone had an AUC of 0.779. Combining KAI1 and VEGF improved diagnostic performance, increasing sensitivity to 91.86%, accuracy to 84.68%, and negative predictive value to 78.79%. The authors conclude that combined detection may form a more reliable biomarker panel for HCC than either marker alone.
From Wu Zhang, Cheng-Guang Zhao, Hong-Yu Sun, Wei-E Zheng, and Hua Chen. Expression characteristics of kai1 and vascular endothelial growth factor and their diagnostic value for hepatocellular carcinoma. Gut and Liver, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.5009/gnl13331, doi:10.5009/gnl13331.

pqac-acd98134: The excerpt is about a serum microRNA panel for HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis, not about KAI1 and VEGF. It reports that an 8-miRNA set achieved good diagnostic accuracy with AUC values around 0.887–0.893 for distinguishing HCC from controls and cirrhosis, but it does not mention KAI1, VEGF, or their combined detection, sensitivity, or specificity. Therefore, it provides no direct evidence to answer how combined KAI1+VEGF testing improves HCC diagnosis compared with either marker alone.
From Youwen Tan, Guohong Ge, Tengli Pan, Danfeng Wen, Li Chen, Xuejun Yu, Xinbei Zhou, and Jianhe Gan. A serum microrna panel as potential biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma related with hepatitis b virus. PLoS ONE, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0107986, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0107986.

pqac-d1713da2: The excerpt describes a study on alcohol-enhanced progression and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), showing that alcohol increases ROS, activates NF-κB signaling, and upregulates VEGF and MCP-1, which contribute to tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis. It does not mention KAI1 or the use of KAI1 and VEGF as combined biomarkers for HCC diagnosis, nor does it report diagnostic performance improvements over single-marker testing.
From Fei Wang, Jin-Lian Yang, Ke-ke Yu, Mei Xu, You-zhi Xu, Li Chen, Yan-min Lu, Hao-shu Fang, Xin-yi Wang, Zhong-qian Hu, Fei-fei Li, Lixin Kan, Jia Luo, and Si-Ying Wang. Activation of the nf-κb pathway as a mechanism of alcohol enhanced progression and metastasis of human hepatocellular carcinoma. Molecular Cancer, 2015. URL: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12943-014-0274-0, doi:10.1186/s12943-014-0274-0.
